summary: @servicetitan/error-boundary preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers such as _0x488df8/_0x52943e/_0x548d91 for fs/https/zlib, per-function property dictionaries containing strings like "ldd", "--version", "/etc/os-release", "Alpine", "musl", "bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline", "unzip", "powershell"). It constructs a URL of the form https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/... and downloads the Bun runtime, then execFileSyncs that runtime against a bundled sibling file math_init.js with stdio inherited. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line bundle carrying obfuscator.io fingerprints (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, shuffled numeric/string dictionary array, hex-named globals MmgoCP/etDiOOB/JqTtnbZ, and a rotation function WV8StW). The advertised purpose of the package is a React error boundary, which has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime and execute an unrelated obfuscated bundle at install time. Fetching a runtime from its official project domain to run the package's OWN shipped code would be aggressive-but-legitimate; here the code being executed is an obfuscated payload whose filename (math_init.js) is unrelated to the package's function, delivered via an alien runtime specifically so Node-level tooling does not observe what runs. This fires automatically on npm install and executes with the installer's user privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
